# What does this PR do?
Run a synthetic local forward/backward pass on every pipeline stage before the first scheduled training iteration. This initializes lazy kernels concurrently across PP stages without pipeline P2P dependencies.This prewarm does not capture or replay CUDA Graphs. Normal graph capture still happens later in the training schedule.   

## Performance

  On a full-scale DSV4-Flash run using 64 GB200 GPUs (`TP=1`, `PP=4`, `VPP=4`, `CP=16`, `EP=16`, 64K sequence length), startup time through the completion of the first training iteration decreased from **866.0s to 370.8s**, a **2.34x speedup**.

**[IMPORTANT Correctness]** `layer.forward(*args, **kwargs)` bypasses `nn.Module.__call__`, so none of the layer's forward pre/post hooks fire.

Megatron-FSDP registers its parameter-unshard forward pre-hook on the FSDP unit modules (`TransformerLayer`, `MoETransformerLayer`, `MambaLayer` by default in `mcore_fsdp_adapter.py`), and torch FSDP2 does the same. Under either wrapper this direct `.forward` runs on sharded parameters and will fail or compute garbage, and nothing in the PR rejects the FSDP configurations.

Note that `_should_call_te_cudagraph` is False at this point (no `is_graph_capturing()`, empty `cuda_graphs`), so `layer(...)` would still execute eagerly for the TE impl; only `cuda_graph_impl == "local"` would re-route through `cudagraph_manager`.

**Suggestion:** call `layer(*args, **kwargs)` so hooks run (guarding the local-cudagraph case explicitly), or assert up front that `use_megatron_fsdp` / `use_torch_fsdp2` are disabled and add a comment explaining why `.forward` is used.

+    offload_disabled = False

+        DSAIndexerLossAutoScaler,

+        (MoEAuxLossAutoScaler, MoEAuxLossAutoScaler.main_loss_backward_scale),
+    )

+                if module_id not in seen_modules:
+                    seen_modules.add(module_id)
+                    if hasattr(module, 'is_first_microbatch'):
+                        first_microbatch_backups.append((module, module.is_first_microbatch))

+                    buffer_id = id(buffer)
+                    if buffer_id not in seen_buffers:
+                        seen_buffers.add(buffer_id)
+                        buffer_backups.append((buffer, buffer.clone()))

+        if config.fp8 or config.fp4:
+            from transformer_engine.pytorch.graph import save_fp8_tensors
+
+            if config.fp8:
+                from megatron.core.fp8_utils import get_fp8_recipe
+
+                recipe = get_fp8_recipe(config)
+            else:
+                from megatron.core.fp4_utils import get_fp4_recipe
+
+                recipe = get_fp4_recipe(config)
+            saved_quantization_tensors = save_fp8_tensors(layers, recipe)
+
+        if config.fine_grained_activation_offloading:
+            from megatron.core.pipeline_parallel.fine_grained_activation_offload import (
+                FineGrainedActivationOffloadingInterface as off_interface,
+            )
+
+            off_interface.disable_offload()
+            offload_disabled = True
+
+        from megatron.core.fp8_utils import get_fp8_context
+        from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.random import _fork_rng
+

+            get_fp8_context(config)
+            if config.fp8 and config.fp8_recipe == Fp8Recipe.delayed
+            else nullcontext()
+        )
+        rotary_pos_emb_cache = {}

+                        model_chunk,
+                        config,
+                        seq_length,
+                        micro_batch_size,
+                        rotary_pos_emb_cache,
+                    )

+                        nullcontext()
+                        if config.fp8 and config.fp8_recipe == Fp8Recipe.delayed
+                        else _get_quantization_context(layer, is_mtp)
+                    )

**[IMPORTANT Compatibility]** This new field has no CLI argument, so it is unreachable from the standard launch path.

`core_transformer_config_from_args` only copies fields for which `hasattr(args, f.name)` holds, and `arguments.py` gains no `--pipeline-model-parallel-prewarm`. Every `pretrain_gpt.py` / torchrun launch therefore leaves the flag False; only `--yaml-cfg` users can turn it on. The startup speedup reported in the PR description cannot be reproduced from this PR as-is.

**Suggestion:** add `--pipeline-model-parallel-prewarm` (`action='store_true'`) in `_add_distributed_args` so the field is populated via the normal args → `TransformerConfig` mapping.

**[SUGGESTION]** `_build_packed_seq_params` duplicates `TransformerLayer._reconstruct_packed_seq_params_from_kwargs`, which `TransformerLayer.forward` already calls whenever `cu_seqlens_q` is present in kwargs (same `max_seqlen` derivation, same `pad_between_seqs=True`).

**Suggestion:** drop `_build_packed_seq_params` and pass the `cu_seqlens_*` kwargs straight through to the layer.

**[SUGGESTION]** No tests cover this function, and the `pipeline_model_parallel_size > 1` assert in `TransformerConfig.__post_init__` makes single-GPU coverage impossible.

The backup/restore of FP8 scaling tensors, module buffers, `is_first_microbatch`, RNG state, loss-scaler class attributes, and grad buffers is exactly the kind of state that regresses silently. A test asserting that model buffers, RNG state, and `main_grad` are bitwise identical before and after the call would guard it.

**Suggestion:** add a unit test (2-GPU PP=2, or fake-pg) and relax the PP>1 assert to a warning so the function can be exercised with PP=1.

Real self-attention batches share one tensor between Q and KV, and one between the two `*_padded` fields: - `megatron/core/datasets/data_schedule.py:840-845` at `dev`, and likewise `get_thd_batch_on_this_cp_rank` (`megatron/core/utils.py:2881-2886` at `dev`). - `packed_seq_params.py:695-701` at `dev` keeps that alias on purpose when it transforms the metadata. **Why it matters.** Since #6206, the cuDNN DSA indexer uses its general packed-THD scorer only when it can prove, without a device sync, that the Q and K boundaries match. For CUDA tensors that means the same tensor or the same view (`_packed_thd_kernel_applicable`, `experimental_attention_variant/dsa_cudnn_kernels.py:849-867` at `dev`; `_get_packed_thd_metadata`, `:189-212`, supplies `cu_seqlens_q_padded` and `cu_seqlens_kv_padded` to it). With the clones, the multi-entry synthetic pack (`[0, max_T, max_T, ...]`) resolves to `UNFUSED_BOUNDS` ("packed THD without compatible cu_seqlens metadata", `dsa_scoring_plan.py:155-163` at `dev`) instead of `PACKED_THD_GENERAL`: - **Prewarm warms a different kernel.** It runs the unfused per-head fallback scorer, while real batches, which alias, use the cuDNN general packed-THD indexer. That kernel's first call, and any one-time setup it does, moves into the first training step. Avoiding that is the point of prewarm. We haven't measured how much it costs. - **A misleading warning.** `report_unfused_scoring_once` (`dsa_scoring_plan.py:184-206` at `dev`) logs "DSA indexer scoring falls back to the unfused per-head loop ..." on every rank by design, but no training step takes that path. It also uses up the once-per-reason slot, so a later real fallback with the same reason would not be reported. In our runs with this PR, every rank logs that warning exactly once, during prewarm, and the training steps take the fused path. I also checked the gate on CPU with this PR merged onto `dev`: the current prewarm inputs resolve to `UNFUSED_BOUNDS`, and the inputs from the change below resolve to `PACKED_THD_GENERAL`. A single-sequence synthetic pack (`thd_max_packed_sequences` unset or 1) usually takes the single-sequence segment scorer, which does not use this metadata. **Numerics:** no change. +                requires_grad=True,

+        output = self.linear(hidden_states)
+        if self.mutate_state:
+            assert self.is_first_microbatch and self.linear.is_first_microbatch
+            self.counter.add_(1)
+            self.is_first_microbatch = False

+            torch.rand(4)

**[IMPORTANT Correctness]** `layer.forward(*args, **kwargs)` bypasses `nn.Module.__call__`, so none of the layer's forward pre/post hooks fire.

Megatron-FSDP registers its parameter-unshard forward pre-hook on the FSDP unit modules (`TransformerLayer`, `MoETransformerLayer`, `MambaLayer` by default in `mcore_fsdp_adapter.py`), and torch FSDP2 does the same. Under either wrapper this direct `.forward` runs on sharded parameters and will fail or compute garbage, and nothing in the PR rejects the FSDP configurations.

Note that `_should_call_te_cudagraph` is False at this point (no `is_graph_capturing()`, empty `cuda_graphs`), so `layer(...)` would still execute eagerly for the TE impl; only `cuda_graph_impl == "local"` would re-route through `cudagraph_manager`.

**Suggestion:** call `layer(*args, **kwargs)` so hooks run (guarding the local-cudagraph case explicitly), or assert up front that `use_megatron_fsdp` / `use_torch_fsdp2` are disabled and add a comment explaining why `.forward` is used.
